title: Mining Engineering, B.S. (College of Earth and Mineral Sciences)
notes: Built from the archived 2023-24 bulletin (raw HTML fetched and cross-checked against its own printed subtotals, not just WebFetch's summary). Program Requirements table: 131 total credits. Course-by-course diff against the 2022-23 archive (MINE-2022.json) found only one cosmetic text difference in the Requirements table itself (PHIL/STS 233's title 'Ethics and the Design of Technology' now resolves where it didn't in 2022's scrape) -- the prescribed-course list, all eight Additional-Courses elective categories (A-H), and the 131-credit total are otherwise byte-identical to 2022-23. The one REAL, substantive change versus 2022-23 is in the Suggested Academic Plan tab: the Second Year Spring statistics slot switches from 2022-23's 'STAT 301 (If STAT 301 not available, take STAT 401 instead)' to 'EME 210 or STAT 401' -- the same pairing MINE-2026.json already uses, three years earlier than the live 2026 edition. (The Requirements table's own Prescribed Courses list still literally shows 'STAT 301' unchanged in this 2023-24 archive -- same table-vs-suggested-plan inconsistency the live 2026 bulletin still has today; the Suggested Academic Plan, which is what this JSON's semester sequence is built from, is what actually changed.) Modeled here as options ['STAT 401', 'EME 210'], STAT 401 first, identical reasoning and ordering to MINE-2026.json's own note: MNG 412 later in this plan has a real current-catalog prereq on STAT 401 specifically (Backend/catalogs/mng_catalog.json), so EME 210 must not be preferred first. Every other Requirements-table category (CMPSC 201/202, EME 301/ME 300, CE 360/EME 303, GEOSC 470W/MNG 470) matches the live 2026 bulletin's 'Elective Categories' table exactly, so MINE-2026.json's own handbook-verification fixes apply unchanged here too: modeled as ME 300 (the Suggested Plan text itself still says 'EME 301 or ME 201', same known table-vs-plan mismatch as every year checked, not a 2023-specific bug), CE 360 added alongside EME 303 (never mentioned in the Suggested Plan text itself, only the Requirements table, in any year checked), and CMPSC 203 dropped from the CMPSC 200/201 pairing. MNG 223: like 2022-23, MNG 223 ('Mineral Land and Mine Surveying') still resolves to a real title in this 2023-24 archive's Requirements table (title is lost starting the 2024-25 archive, see MINE-2024.json) -- but since Backend/catalogs/mng_catalog.json (the engine's single, current-day course catalog, not year-scoped) has never had MNG 223, CE 209 (the bulletin's own listed 'MNG 223 or CE 209' alternate) is used exclusively, same substitution as every other year. Same real CHEM 110 -> MATH 22 -> MATH 21 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 3 hidden-prereq chain documented in MINE-2026.json's notes applies identically here (current-catalog-driven, not year-specific) -- MATH 3/4/21/22 added across Semesters 1-4 for the same reason. Term placement within the 3rd year matches 2022-23 exactly, not 2024-26: MNG 404 and the GHW Gen Ed sit in Fall alongside EE 211, GEOSC 201, and the EME 460/MNG 412 alternative; ENGL 202C and a Knowledge Domain Gen Ed sit in Spring alongside MNPR 301, MNG 422, MNG 331, and MNG 441 (this flips starting the 2024-25 archive, annotated '(FALL ONLY)'/'(SPRING ONLY)' there -- see MINE-2024.json). Reproduced in Semesters 5-6 below, with MNG 412 added as its own standalone Semester-6 item for the same real MNG 451W capstone AND-chain reason (MNG 331 + MNG 404 + MNG 412 + MNG 422) MINE-2026.json's notes document -- the 2023-24 Suggested Plan itself still only lists 'MNG 412 (Take MNG 412 in place of EME 460)' as one alternative pick. 'At which campus can I study this program?' section of this archived page: Begin Campus 'Any Penn State Campus', End Campus 'University Park' only, same as every other year checked (2022 through live 2026) -- see MINE-2026.json for this major's full campus-check finding. The 'Mining Engineering, B.S. at Commonwealth Campuses' Suggested Academic Plan on this same page (132 total credits) is unchanged from 2022-23's version.
